children: 1025 ET - The combined earnings of the energy companies that are part of the S&P 500 stock index more than doubled during 3Q compared with the same period of last year, according to financial-data provider London Stock Exchange Group. As a result, energy accounted for the highest earnings growth in 3Q among all sectors represented in the benchmark, followed by technology, with about 71% combined earnings growth, and materials, with 32%, LSEG's data shows. By comparison, the combined earnings of all companies in the index rose 34% in 3Q from a year earlier. Technology, however, was the S&P 500's sector that recorded the highest revenue growth-about 42%-during 3Q, followed by energy and communications services, with 36% and 14% respectively. (luis.garcia@wsj.com; @lhvgarcia)

0949 ET - Crude futures are higher for a third session, but on track for weekly losses as increasing supply offsets emerging concerns about the lack of progress toward a Middle East conflict settlement. In its monthly report, the IEA said it expects global supply to return to a surplus in 4Q. The Paris-based agency estimates that supply will be down by 4.8 million barrels a day in all of 2026, and recover by 6.6 million b/d a day in 2027. Demand is seen falling by 2.7 million b/d this year, and picking up by 2 million b/d next, the IEA said. WTI is up 0.8% at $89.41 a barrel and Brent is up 1.2% at $96.94 a barrel. (anthony.harrup@wsj.com)

0916 ET - Futures markets price in a Fed hike in December, with some bets on a jumbo increase of half a percentage point. A hawkish Fed bodes well for the dollar, as "persistently-wide rate differentials look likely to keep the dollar supported until the end of the year," Corpay's Karl Schamotta says in a note, adding that "further gains could be hard-won." He sees the currency as overbought against the euro, pound, yen and Canadian dollar and "vulnerable to an eventual reset in expectations." The WSJ Dollar Index rises slightly. (paulo.trevisani@wsj.com; @ptrevisani)

0855 ET - The dollar weakens slightly against a basket of currencies as the U.S. October Producer Price Index comes in lower than expected. PPI was 0.3%, versus WSJ consensus of 0.4% and lower than September's 1.4%. The reading eases inflation fears that have boosted expectations of fast interest rate increases by the Fed and, consequently, lifted the dollar to recent highs. The DXY dollar index falls to 103.14 from 103.19 before the inflation data. The dollar is stable against the euro and the yen. (paulo.trevisani@wsj.com; @ptrevisani)

0846 ET - Treasury yields fall on cooler-than-expected U.S. producer inflation. October PPI comes in at 0.3%, slower than WSJ consensus of 0.4% and from September's upwardly revised 1.4% pace. The data follows higher-than-expected consumer inflation, which triggered a sharp increase in yields. Futures markets price in a Fed hike in December. The 10-year yield slips to 5.127% from 5.145% before the PPI numbers. The two-year declines to 4.836% from 4.876%. (paulo.trevisani@wsj.com; @ptrevisani)

0748 ET - This week's Microsoft outage exposes the risk of placing an entire organization's communications within the cloud of a single provider, says Benjamin Schilz, chief executive of communications platform Wire. "No one should be pointing fingers at Microsoft right now. Technology is never perfect, and an outage like this could happen to any business, including us," he says. But he adds that government agencies, the defense sector and critical infrastructure cannot afford to depend on a single service for their communications. "Digital sovereignty means more than just having control over data and where it is stored; it also means remaining operational during a disruption," he says. "If an organization makes all its communications dependent on one platform, it effectively ties its crisis-response capability to that same platform." (edith.hancock@wsj.com)

0735 ET - Microsoft says it's seeing encouraging recovery progress, with service availability and email delivery performance improving across a growing portion of affected Microsoft 365 infrastructure. "Some users may still experience intermittent issues as recovery actions continue," the company says in a post on X. "We're focused on recovery for the remaining affected environments while prioritizing email queue and backlog reduction." The comments come as Microsoft continues working to resolve an outage that has disrupted services including Outlook and Teams for hundreds of thousands of users since Thursday. Microsoft off 1.5% premarket. (connor.hart@wsj.com)

0702 ET - Microsoft says it has made additional progress toward recovery in the wake of a widespread outage that has affected hundreds of thousands of users. The company says recovery actions have been completed across portions of affected infrastructure, with traffic being gradually restored. "We're seeing improvements in key scenarios, including mailbox access and delayed email processing, though some intermittent issues may continue," the company says in a post on X. "Our focus is extending these recovery actions across remaining affected infrastructure while continuing stabilization and adding capacity to improve consistency." Microsoft slips 1.4% premarket. (connor.hart@wsj.com)

0701 ET - Nvidia's third-quarter results next week will be closely watched for any near-term direction on the chip company's share price after Jensen Huang's resignation, XTB's Kathleen Brooks writes. "While we expect another monster report and we fully expect earnings to come in above estimates of $108 billion, it's the future outlook that is more important than ever for Nvidia's share price," Brooks says. Shares are up 2.5% at $170.35 in premarket trading, having fallen 4.34% in the earlier session. They are currently down 19% over the month-to-date. (ian.walker@wsj.com)

0302 ET - Novo Nordisk stands ready to launch new obesity and diabetes jab CagriSema, a rollout which must prove that a renaissance in obesity injectables is achievable and that semaglutide-patent expiries are surmountable, Berenberg analysts write. Assuming obesity-treatment approval by year-end, Novo stands ready to launch CagriSema in the U.S. in early 2027, the bank says. Novo's injectable business remains lackluster as competitor Eli Lilly continues to dominate market-share gains. At the same time, investor sentiment on the upcoming CagriSema launch remains subdued, it adds. However, Novo delivered solid third-quarter results and a guidance upgrade. Wegovy pill continues to surprise on the upside, and new market launches should see strong growth carry into 2027. The bank has a hold rating on the stock and 305 Danish kroner price target. Shares closed at 275.75 kroner. (dominic.chopping@wsj.com)
